media_work.focus_or_theme: Memoir of Jim McCloskey's work with Centurion Ministries freeing the wrongfully convicted

key_quotes_raw: "A riveting and infuriating examination of criminal prosecutions, revealing how easy it is to convict the wrong person and how nearly impossible it is to undo the error." —Washington Post
"[Exoneration] takes an advocate who is tireless, fearless, and dedicated to justice. A man like Jim McCloskey, the dean of all innocence advocates—The Exonerator" —from the foreword by John Grisham
"No one has illuminated this problem more thoughtfully and persistently than Rev. McCloskey and his extraordinary team at Centurion." —Bryan Stevenson, author of Just Mercy
systemic_issues_raw: Ease of wrongful convictions in the American justice system
Reliance on witness testimony that may be false or coerced
Racial bias in the criminal justice system
policy_recommendations_raw: Better systems for reviewing potential wrongful convictions
Improved support for exonerees after release
Greater accountability for prosecutors and police who contribute to wrongful convictions

media_item.item_title: Book Content: When Truth Is All You Have: A Memoir of Faith, Justice, and Freedom for the Wrongly Convicted
media_item.focus_or_theme: Memoir of Jim McCloskey's work with Centurion Ministries freeing the wrongfully convicted
media_item.summary_notes: A memoir detailing Jim McCloskey's journey from a management consultant to a leading advocate for the wrongfully convicted, focusing on his work with Centurion Ministries and highlighting various cases, systemic issues within the justice system, and policy recommendations for reform.  The book also explores McCloskey's personal and spiritual journey.
media_item.case_details_raw: The book features several cases handled by Centurion Ministries, including that of Jorge de los Santos (the first case that inspired McCloskey), Clarence Brandley (where perjured testimony played a role), and Walter McMillian (also featured in Bryan Stevenson's "Just Mercy").  Specific details about the crimes, convictions, and sentences are not provided in the available source.

research_notes_raw:
Jim McCloskey founded Centurion Ministries in 1983, the first organization in America devoted to overturning wrongful convictions. His journey began when he was a chaplain at Trenton State Prison in 1980, where he met Jorge de los Santos, who claimed innocence. After investigating the case, McCloskey became convinced of de los Santos's innocence and worked to free him.

The book chronicles McCloskey's journey from a former management consultant who enrolled at Princeton Theological Seminary at the age of 37 to becoming one of the foremost advocates for the wrongfully convicted. John Grisham, who wrote the foreword to the book, calls McCloskey "the dean of all innocence advocates."

The memoir details not only the cases McCloskey worked on but also the personal and spiritual journey that led him to dedicate his life to freeing the innocent. The book has been praised for its compassionate portrayal of the wrongfully convicted and its illumination of flaws in the criminal justice system.
